sites.name: The last ghetto wall (Király utca 15)
sites.why: A memorial section of the Budapest ghetto wall, rebuilt in 2010 in the courtyard where the last piece of the original 1944–45 wall stood until 2006. The sealed Pest ghetto, about 70,000 people, ran from late November 1944 until Soviet liberation on 17–18 January 1945. A place to visit, on the same street as Helen's wartime home at number 6

journey.name: Tiszabogdány / Bohdan (home)
journey.why: The family village and Helen's birthplace (Helman + Lando). Roza and the children were rounded up here on 16 April 1944

journey.name: Mátészalka ghetto
journey.why: Where the whole Rakhiv district, Roza and the children, were held before Auschwitz

journey.name: Szatmár (Satu Mare): the Katz home
journey.why: The origin and home town of the Katz family, Tibi's family (4 Kossuth Lajos utca), as Bogdan was for the Helmans. In 1944 the town's Jews were held in the Satu Mare ghetto and deported to Auschwitz in May and June 1944

journey.name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
journey.why: Where Roza and five children (Photo 133) and the Satu Mare relatives were murdered on arrival, 26 May 1944

journey.name: Kassa / Košice (the counting)
journey.why: On 22 May 1944 the sealed transport from the Mátészalka ghetto was counted through Kassa on its way to Auschwitz, 3,298 people on board. The date and the number survive because the Kassa railway station logged every deportation train that passed through

journey.name: Buchenwald
journey.why: Where Zacharias, Michal, and Lajos were registered after Auschwitz, on 2 June 1944, and held in the tent camp (the Zeltlager, block Z-4) before the men were sent on to the labour subcamps

journey.name: Magdeburg-Rothensee (subcamp)
journey.why: Zacharias's slave-labour subcamp; sent back to Auschwitz and killed October 1944

journey.name: Rehmsdorf / Tröglitz (subcamp)
journey.why: Michal Helman's subcamp (the 'Wille' fuel plant) before Theresienstadt

journey.name: Fünfteichen (subcamp)
journey.why: Jenő Helman and his son Mordekhai; Jenő died here about January 1945

journey.name: Terezín / Theresienstadt
journey.why: Where Michal and Lajos Helman were liberated, 8 May 1945

journey.name: Dachau
journey.why: Szerene Sperber (Helen's cousin, née Müller) imprisoned here; she survived

journey.name: Bergen-Belsen
journey.why: Where little Eva was deported after the death march; as a small child she shared a bunk with a corpse, and survived

journey.name: Thorn / Toruń
journey.why: Where Tibi was held about a month AFTER the war, in a camp then holding German POWs, for border-crossing

journey.name: Ainring (DP camp)
journey.why: Tibi's displaced-persons camp, December 1945 to February 1947, before he crossed to Palestine

journey.name: Kloster Indersdorf
journey.why: The children's centre on Helen's postwar path out of Europe

journey.name: Prien am Chiemsee
journey.why: The children's programme Helen's DP card was falsified two years younger to join

journey.name: Bremerhaven
journey.why: Where Helen sailed for America on the SS Marine Marlin, May 1947

journey.name: Uzhhorod (Ungvár), Minajská 27
journey.why: Where four of Miksa and Hani's children (Bumi, Jakab, Herman/Tzvi, Sara) settled for city work in 1936-37, all at this one address; the Czechoslovak state registered them as Polish 'foreigners' because nationality passed from their grandfather Iczik of Delatyn, even for the children born in Bogdan

journey.name: Kolozsvár (Cluj): Eva's birthplace
journey.why: Where Eva (Sándor Katz and Margit Roth's daughter) was born in 1938, as listed on her postwar DP card. Bookmarked here until the exact street address is confirmed from Rosie's memoir

journey.name: Delatyn (Delyatyn)
journey.why: The family's paternal origin, in Galicia (now Ukraine). Iczik Helman and Feige Dikker both came from here; the family's Polish nationality passed down from Delatyn, even to the children born in Bogdan

journey.name: Stalingrad (the eastern front)
journey.why: David Helman, Zacharias's brother, fled east into the Soviet Union in 1939, joined the Red Army, and fell at Stalingrad, on the Soviet side of the front, about 1943

journey.name: The River Don (the eastern front)
journey.why: Where the Hungarian Second Army and its unarmed Jewish forced-labour companies (the munkaszolgálat) were destroyed in the winter of 1942 to 1943. Yosef and Moshe Helman, Miksa's sons, were forced labourers here, not armed soldiers, on the Axis side against the Soviets, and died on the Don

specialMarkers.label: Reitzenhain: the train was attacked
specialMarkers.title: Reitzenhain: where the train was attacked
specialMarkers.detail: At Reitzenhain station, on the Saxon–Bohemian border, Allied fighter-bombers strafed the evacuation train in mid-April 1945. In the panic that followed, about 380 prisoners were hunted down and shot near the town; a memorial by the tracks holds the reburied victims. The survivors, Michal and Lajos among them, were then marched on foot to Terezín.

specialMarkers.label: Margit: shot here, early
specialMarkers.title: Approximate: where Margit was shot
specialMarkers.detail: On what should have been Eva's first day of school, both of them dressed for it, the Arrow Cross seized Margit and little Eva as they left home. They were carrying forged Christian papers, but the person who had sold them those papers informed on them. Forced onto the death march west through rain and mud, Margit could not walk in her heels. She was told that if walking was too hard a wagon would come for her, so she stood waiting for the wagon, and was shot where she stood. Eva, beside her, heard the shot but did not see it, and understood only afterward. Eva was deported on to Bergen-Belsen, where she survived. This point is an approximation on the documented route; the exact spot is unknown.

specialMarkers.label: Tibi: feigned death and escaped here
specialMarkers.title: Approximate: where Tibi feigned death and escaped
specialMarkers.detail: On the second night of the death march he feigned death, rolled into a roadside ditch among the bodies, lay in the mud until the column passed, then walked back toward Budapest. He made it to the end of the second day, roughly 55 to 65 km northwest of the city along this route; this point is an approximation, the exact spot is unknown.
